cover.headline: 12 stories in 5 minutes. Iran ties Hormuz to its terms, the US votes Tuesday, Zelensky offers to meet Putin.

stories.head: Iran: Hormuz could reopen in two days, on its terms
body: Foreign Minister Araghchi says the strait could reopen within two days if Washington accepts Tehran's conditions, including lifting the blockade of its ports.
Trump says the US is in no hurry and has one or two sites to deal with. Khamenei has told commanders to prepare.

stories.head: Zelensky offers to meet Putin in Turkey
body: Per ANSA, citing RBC-Ukraine and Turkish CNN, he wants talks on a ceasefire, monitoring and security guarantees. He rejects ceding the Donbas.
Russia's statistics agency Rosstat confirms a cyberattack. Hackers claim war-casualty data; Rosstat denies any theft.

stories.head: US votes Tuesday, Bolsonaro in Miami, Delhi rallies
body: US: all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are up; polls favor Democrats in the House. Rubio says the US did not help Flavio Bolsonaro leave Brazil.
India: thousands rallied demanding the election chief resign over voter-roll cuts. Israel: Herzog's talks start Nov. 4.

stories.head: Gaza strikes, French blockades, Frankfurt riots
body: Gaza: at least eight killed Sunday despite the ceasefire, hospital sources say. The toll since 2023 tops 74,500.
France: school blockades resume after a third weekend of marches. Frankfurt: looting and fires, 30 detained.

stories.head: COP31 opens Nov. 9 without the US
body: Current pledges cut emissions only 11% to 15% by 2035. About 45% is needed to reach 1.5C, UNEP says.
Seoul: President Lee urges a new growth formula as the KOSPI opens down 1.6% on chip jitters.
